# Biomarkers and Registry 2.0

Registry 2.0 has 113 typed measurement definitions across 83 analytes and 637 EN/RU/ES aliases. Definition identity is analyte plus specimen, property, scale, timing, method, and value kind.

## Actual lifecycle

`worker/src/pipeline.ts` extracts laboratory rows with `extractPipelineBiomarkersFromText` or `extractPipelineBiomarkersFromImage` and first inserts raw evidence into `document_extracted_biomarkers` with `status='needs_review'`: raw label, numeric/text value, unit/raw unit, `document_id`, `profile_id`, and source page/text. A clinical axis such as specimen can be preserved only when its lexical form is captured with that row's source text or section context; an omitted structured field may be recovered from that captured row evidence, but the system never fabricates an unstated axis. Initial extraction does not call `resolveMeasurementDefinition` and does not persist a resolver outcome. `document_type` remains on `documents.document_type`, not on an extracted or observation row.

`GET /api/documents/[id]/biomarkers` returns the raw extracted row and computes a `buildNormalizationReview` preview. Preview is not persistence. Explicit acceptance (`POST .../biomarkers/accept`), correction or confirmation (`PATCH .../biomarkers`), and operator Registry batch reprocessing use `writeExtractedBiomarkerNormalization`, which calls `write_observation_normalization_revision_v2`. Each persists one source-linked observation and an active normalization revision for `resolved`, `partial`, `ambiguous`, or `unmapped`: raw evidence and document linkage remain on the observation; result/trace remain on the revision and project back to the extracted row.
The review UI draws a source-region overlay only for persisted, page-coherent exact positional provenance on the displayed page. Fuzzy, ambiguous, model-origin, cross-page, legacy, missing-layer, and invalid regions remain page-only so the UI never presents an unverified rectangle as fact; pointer hover and keyboard focus do not navigate or scroll, while explicit selection retains the page affordance.

## Resolver outcomes and consumers

| outcome | concrete definition | verification | default record lifecycle | Health Profile |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `resolved` | concrete reviewed definition | `user_verified` on acceptance; `auto_verified` only from the approved service quality gate | `active` | eligible only when verified, numeric, source-range-backed, and covered by a reviewed compatible binding |
| `partial` | none; analyte tier only if supplied by resolver | `pending` | `active` until an explicit lifecycle transition | not eligible |
| `ambiguous` | none; analyte tier only if supplied by resolver | `pending` | `active` until an explicit lifecycle transition | not eligible |
| `unmapped` | none | `pending` | `active` until an explicit lifecycle transition | not eligible |

## Document review and lifecycle

`GET /api/documents/[id]/biomarkers` and document bootstrap responses expose `recordStatus`, `sourceIsCurrent`, persisted or preview `traceState`, and `actionAvailability`. The review UI renders resolver outcome, verification status, and record lifecycle as independent labels. Raw acceptance keeps incomplete evidence without verification; rejection requires an owner-scoped reason and current source/revision confirmation; automatic verification is service-only. Once every current published extracted row leaves `needs_review` or `pending_review`, the acceptance endpoint transitions the document from `needs_review` to `ready` / `completed`; a partial acceptance leaves the document reviewable and the action available.

`rejected` and `superseded` are record-lifecycle states, not verification statuses. Their source rows remain available as historical/raw evidence with stable non-PII reason codes, but are read-only and excluded from current observation, batch-verification, correction, reversal, and Health Profile projections. Reprocessing supersedes laboratory sources through the lifecycle seam instead of deleting raw evidence or normalization history.

## Health Profile projection

`GET /api/health-profile` admits laboratory input only through `projectHealthProfileLaboratoryInput`. The source must be current and active, have an active `resolved` trace whose selected candidate matches the measurement definition, use reviewed Registry v2 provenance, have a reviewed compatible assessment binding, and be `auto_verified`, `user_verified`, or `manually_corrected`. Its value must be finite and numeric, and its source document must retain a non-blank printed reference range with at least one finite non-inverted boundary. `GET /api/biomarkers` returns a stable assessment exclusion reason and safe non-inclusion guidance when any gate fails; it does not call the source laboratory result invalid. Registry, population, and generic ranges are never substituted. Once admitted, score role, specimen, readiness group, and contribution group policies still govern scoring. A named system receives a numeric current-state score only when every approved readiness group has one usable `core` alternative; a missing group returns an ordered `missing` reason, and a present but unusable group returns `invalid`. Neither case produces a partial score or `0`. Incomplete, rejected, superseded, provisional, unverified, qualitative, range-ineligible, or non-laboratory observations remain readable evidence but do not enter the scored profile. New assessments carry a stable score algorithm version plus per-system readiness groups, selected score contributors, source page/region evidence, and explicit exclusion reasons; these explanations are descriptive and never replace the factual observation record. Legacy cached assessments without provenance remain readable without fabricated explanations until regenerated.

Chart-facing `GET /api/biomarkers` and `GET /api/health-profile` responses emit `Cache-Control: no-store`, so corrections are not served from an HTTP cache. Health Profile reads the latest assessment, job, and synthesis state without generating synthesis during `GET`. When a persisted assessment has a non-succeeded recalculation job, the response reports `assessment_freshness: "outdated"`, returns `null` named-system and overall scores, and adds an `outdated` readiness reason to every named system while retaining factual source evidence.

## Unknown labels and controlled reprocessing

An unknown label remains raw extracted evidence and becomes persisted `unmapped` only after acceptance or explicit Registry batch reprocessing. `scripts/reprocess-batch.ts` invokes the operator-controlled batch path. There is no HTTP Registry-batch endpoint, automatic catalog-change reprocessing, automatic catalog growth from patient or LLM input, admin queue promoting unknown labels, or source-document-to-catalog provenance promotion.

## Locales, units, and legacy

Aliases carry explicit EN/RU/ES locale metadata. Russian uses Unicode-aware label normalization; Spanish accent-fold fallback is collision-gated. Laboratory restrictions never replace locale metadata. Missing units follow each definition policy; conversions are reviewed presentation rules and do not erase raw evidence.

Registry v1 is frozen compatibility history. The authoritative [v1.0.0 audit](../../registry/biomarker-registry/v1.0.0/AUDIT.md) holds its 113 concepts; this guide does not duplicate them. A v1 item is never automatically promoted, admitted as an alias, or used as a runtime fallback.
